label: input z; or steps after an early v (orig 0/1) up to <DEL>; or outputting v
explanation: Two unrelated token-identity components. (1) Input token z: 75% of z steps fire, about 60% of activation mass, and z steps account for the strongest activations (top examples peak at z in the original phase, around t=3-5). z fed back during the copy phase fires less reliably and more weakly. (2) Sequences that open with v (orig(0)=v gives 7.7x lift; orig(1)=v also counts): the feature stays on at a moderate level (about 0.2-0.6 of max) on each original-phase step from t=2 through <DEL>, then fades during copy, where it fires mostly on the steps that output v. It does not fire on v itself as input, on the first two steps, or on ordinary letters or digits in sequences with no v or z. Activation is largest when both components coincide (z inside a v-led sequence). Precision is limited (about 0.65) because many z steps late in the copy phase and some v-led steps stay silent.
